newsitem.title: FRANCE: French UDF leader favours balanced budget law.
newsitem.headline: French UDF leader favours balanced budget law.

text.p: UDF party leader Francois Leotard said in a newspaper interview published on Monday that he favoured legislation requiring a balanced budget within four or five years.

Leotard told Les Echos a law requiring the government to balance the budget, barring a serious crisis, was needed to bring down public spending. "Why impose that rule on municipalities and not on the state?" he said.
The UDF is the junior party in the ruling conservative coalition.

Leotard said better management of the public sector and a re-examination of the state's role in the economy after an audit should lower spending and could reduce the public payroll by more than the 5,000 jobs per year announced by Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

He reiterated the conservative coalition's objective to reduce social charges on employment but added that the new government's first actions after the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election probably should not come "on the fiscal side".
The government is trying to bring the deficit this year to three percent of gross domestic product to fulfil Maastricht treaty criteria for entry to European monetary union.
